newsitem.title: UK: Virgin in talks with other European airlines.
newsitem.headline: Virgin in talks with other European airlines.

text.p: British entrepreneur Richard Branson's European shorthaul airline Virgin Express is talking to several other continental carriers to expand its network through franchising or takeovers, industry sources said on Monday.
One proposal is for Virgin to get access to the British market by linking up with Belgian flag carrier Sabena to operate or share flights between Belgium and Britain, they said.

The sources said Branson was also considering whether to make a counter bid for troubled French airline Air Liberte against arch rival British Airways and was looking at another possible deal in Italy.
Virgin said it is in talks with several airlines but declined to confirm specific proposals, which are bound by confidentiality agreements.

"We are talking to a number of airlines at the moment about opportunities to operate routes for them and even acquire assets but we are talking to several parties and it will be some time before any announcements are made," a senior official said.
Branson said last week he was hatching plans to break into the British short-haul market with Virgin Express.

Virgin Express was created in April with Branson's takeover of European regional carrier EuroBelgian Airlines SA for 38 million sterling ($59.44 million), with the declared aim of undercutting major operators on European routes.

Five months ago, Virgin said the British shorthaul market was already highly competitive compared with the rest of Europe and its main target for expansion would be overpriced mainland routes dominated by national carriers.
But Branson said last week he had decided he also wanted to move in on his home market as well as stirring up the mainland markets with the launch of new cut-price services.

"In Europe it is now possible to create a real pan-European airline which can really take the major airlines apart and it has been great fun so far doing that, reducing fares and still making a profit," he told Reuters in an interview.
"It has been very satisfying but the problem is we have not been able to connect Britain yet...and that is something that we may have more to say about soon," he said.

Sabena is owned 49 percent by Swissair. Virgin has been battling with the Swiss aviation authorities to be allowed to launch a new service from Brussels to Geneva, which would undercut the basic fares currently offered by Swissair and Sabena by 50 percent.
